tool_input.command:
cat >> db/schema.ts <<'EOF'

export const postRevisions = sqliteTable('post_revisions', {
  id: integer('id').primaryKey({ autoIncrement: true }),
  postId: integer('post_id')
    .notNull()
    .references(() => posts.id),
  title: text('title').notNull(),
  excerpt: text('excerpt').notNull(),
  body: text('body').notNull(),
  createdAt: text('created_at').notNull().$defaultFn(() => new Date().toISOString()),
})
EOF
bun run db:make -- --name post_revisions 2>&1 | tail -15; git status --short

result:
Post revisions are implemented: `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass. I didn't add tests for the new routes, so the 404 for a revision on the wrong post and the 403/redirect behaviour are untested. The 404 relies on the ORM's `ModelNotFoundException` (which carries status 404) being mapped to a 404 response by the framework, and I didn't confirm that.

- **Storage:** there is a new `post_revisions` table (`id`, `post_id`, `title`, `excerpt`, `body`, `created_at`). It's defined in `db/schema.ts`, and the generated migration is `db/migrations/20260929140113_bouncy_red_skull`. The `PostRevision` model is in `app/Models/PostRevision.ts`.
- **Keeping versions:** `PostController.update` saves the post's old title, excerpt and body as a revision once the input is validated and the author is authorised. Refused edits and post creation keep nothing. A save that changes nothing still keeps a revision, which the task said it doesn't check.
- **History and restore:** `GET /posts/:id/revisions` renders the new `posts/Revisions` page with `revisions` (`id`, `title`, `createdAt`), newest first. `POST /posts/:id/revisions/:revisionId/restore` keeps the current version as a new revision, puts the chosen one back and redirects to `/posts/:id`. The restored revision stays in the list.
- **Access:** both routes are in the auth group and use the existing update policy. Non-authors get 403 and guests are sent to `/login`. A revision belonging to another post returns 404 without changing anything.
- **Delete:** `destroy` removes the post's revisions before deleting the post.
- **UI:** the post page has a "History" link for the author, and the revisions page (`resources/js/pages/posts/Revisions.tsx`) has a Restore button per revision.

I regenerated the `.guren` codegen files for the new routes and page. The routes are in `routes/web.ts`, and the params validator is in `PostValidator.ts`.
